variants.name: std::optional member guarded by std::call_once
variants.implementation_notes: The value holder is an explicit member: keep std::optional<T> (or a pointer plus flag) next to the identifier and fill it in the accessor under a std::once_flag, so the load runs at most once even for objects shared across threads. Single-threaded holders drop the flag and test optional::has_value(); std::call_once retries after a throwing initializer, so a transient store failure is not cached. A per-object mutex is the alternative when the load must be retried or refreshed, and because a reference into the optional is invalidated when the holder is reassigned, decide the refresh contract before handing out references.
pitfalls: std::once_flag is neither copyable nor movable, so a holder with a flag member loses its implicit copy/move operations; keep deferred members behind a pointer/PIMPL or in a separate holder type.

std::call_once retries after an exception while an optional-plus-flag caches the empty state forever: decide the failure policy explicitly, and remember that dereferencing *optional after a failed load is undefined behaviour.
A reference returned from the holder dangles once the optional is reassigned or reset; return by value or a shared handle when the value can be refreshed.

variants.name: Hand-written proxy class over the subject interface
variants.implementation_notes: The classic EAA form is a stand-in that shares the subject's interface and forwards to the loaded object: the proxy holds the identifier plus a std::unique_ptr<T> and calls the load from the first forwarded member function, so no client ever sees the marker. Choose it when the domain type must stay free of lazy fields, when the subject is polymorphic and callers use it through a base class, or when the load should be triggered by method calls rather than by field access; the price is one forwarding function per operation and an extra indirection on every call.
variants.idiom_name: class implementing the subject interface, loading behind the first forwarded call
pitfalls: Every forwarded member needs the guard (a shared call_once called first is enough): a member that reads the pointer without it dereferences a null unique_ptr.
The proxy is a different type: typeid, dynamic_cast to the concrete author and overload resolution see the proxy, so validate that the interface is genuinely used virtually.

variants.name: Function-local static (magic static) for shared reference data
variants.implementation_notes: For process-wide, immutable reference data the cheapest correct deferral is a function-local static: 'static const Rates r = load_rates();' initializes on the first call, C++11 guarantees the initialization is thread-safe and happens once (the magic-static rule), and the object is destroyed at exit. It is the wrong tool for per-entity rows - one instance per process, not one per object - and a throwing initializer leaves the static uninitialized so the next call retries.
variants.idiom_name: static const T inside the accessor, initialised on first call
pitfalls: The static is one instance for the whole process and lives until exit: it cannot serve per-object lazy rows, and the loaded data is never refreshed.

A re-entrant call from inside the initializer (directly or through another function that calls rates()) is undefined behaviour dressed as a deadlock; a throwing initializer simply retries on the next call.
